source_verification_receipts.version: Statistics and Probability Letters 105 (2015), author manuscript deposited in PMC
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper uses fixed potential outcomes under two-stage randomization, introduces stratified interference, and forms exact scalar-effect confidence sets by inversion of permutation tests.
Conditional multinomial pair counts are binomial; exact pair tests combined by Bonferroni or Holm yield finite-sample rank confidence sets.

The paper specifies complete first-stage assignment to mechanisms and within-cluster randomization, then derives covariance, conservative variance estimation, asymptotic normality, and asymptotic Wald testing.
The paper proves finite-sample tests for partially sharp and bounded individual-level two-saturation nulls and monotonicity, while weak-average inference is asymptotic.
The paper studies empirical-success ranking of saturation policies, deriving finite-sample regret bounds and a quasi-optimal first-stage design rather than confidence coverage.
